WordCraft 

 
 Writing and document design; an open-source, modern word processor, built in pure Rust. 
 

 
 A fast, open-source word processor with a familiar workflow: the ribbon, styles,
 tables, track changes, references and mail merge. It reads and writes .docx, runs natively on
 macOS, Windows, Linux and BSD, and in the browser via WebAssembly. 
 By the ArtCraft team. 
 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 
 
 

 
 WordCraft on getartcraft.com ·
 ArtCraft ·
 All Crafting Apps 
 

 

 
 
 The Open Studio Handbook , WordCraft's built-in sample: the ribbon, live Styles gallery, rulers and the Navigation pane. 
 

 [!NOTE]
 ArtCraft is a community of artists from all walks of life. Painters, photographers,
 filmmakers, illustrators, designers, animators, hobbyists, and people who picked up a pencil
 last week. If you make things, you're one of us. Come say hi on Discord. 

 
 A tour ·
 Why WordCraft ·
 What works today ·
 Quick start ·
 For agents ·
 Architecture ·
 Roadmap ·
 Downloads ·
 The Crafting Apps ·
 License and credits 
 

 A tour

Every screenshot below is WordCraft itself, rendered offscreen by its own UI test harness
( cargo run -p wordcraft-ui-egui --example ui shot ).

 
 
 Review. Track changes, comment balloons in the margin, accept and reject, spelling and grammar as you type. 
 References. Tables of contents, footnotes, citations in APA, MLA, Chicago or IEEE, index and captions. 
 
 
 Design. Themes, style sets, paragraph spacing, watermarks, page colour and borders. 
 Dark mode with formatting marks, and the Insert tab: tables, pictures, shapes, links, headers, footers, fields and symbols. 
 
 
 Layout. Drop caps, text wrapping around pictures and shapes, automatic hyphenation, line numbers and page borders. 
 
 
 File. Start from a template, open recent documents, edit properties, export to PDF and other formats. 
 
 

 Why WordCraft

- Familiar. Ribbon tabs, groups, shortcuts and behaviour: Enter continues a list,
 Tab demotes it, Ctrl/⌘+B bolds the word under the caret, the Styles gallery previews styles live,
 F4 repeats, F7 checks spelling, F8 extends the selection.
- Your files. Opens and saves .docx (OOXML), and also .odt, .rtf, .html, .md, .tex (LaTeX), .txt; opens legacy 97-2003 .doc; exports PDF
 with real, selectable text, links and bookmarks.
- Fast. Paragraph layout is cached, so typing in a 188-page document re-lays it out in about
 1.4 ms; pages render on demand.
- Everywhere. One Rust codebase for macOS, Windows, Linux, BSD and the web. No Electron, no
 Tauri: native egui on the GPU.
- Built for agents. Every action is a command with an id. The same 422 commands drive the
 ribbon, keyboard shortcuts, the command search, a command-line tool, a JSON control channel and
 an MCP server.
- Private. Spelling, grammar and everything else work offline.
- Open. MIT OR Apache-2.0. Clean-room: built from public specifications and observation, with
 every asset original or openly licensed.

 What works today

 Area Highlights 
 --- --- 
 Writing Fast typing with IME, smart quotes, AutoCorrect, list autoformat ( , 1. ), dashes; word, sentence, paragraph selection; drag-select; clipboard with formatting; undo/redo; find and replace with regex 
 Formatting Fonts, sizes, bold/italic/underline styles, strike, sub/superscript, caps, highlight, colours, character spacing, Format Painter, Change Case, Clear Formatting 
 Paragraphs Alignment, indents (draggable on the ruler), spacing, line spacing, tabs with leaders, borders, shading, keep with next, widow/orphan control 
 Styles Built-in style set, live gallery, Styles pane, create/modify/update styles, style sets, themes 
 Lists Bullets, numbering, multilevel, restart, set value, custom formats 
 Tables Insert by grid, merge/split, styles with banded rows, borders, shading, header rows repeated across pages, rows that split across pages, sort, formulas, text ↔ table 
 Pages Margins, orientation, size, columns, page/column/section breaks, headers and footers (first page, odd/even), page numbers, watermark, page borders, line numbers, vertical alignment, drop caps, automatic hyphenation 
 Objects Pictures (resize, crop, recolour, brightness/contrast, transparency, background removal, picture styles, rotate), shapes, text boxes, floating position with text wrapping (square, top and bottom, behind or in front of text) 
 References Table of contents, footnotes and endnotes, citations and bibliography (APA, MLA, Chicago, IEEE), captions, table of figures, cross-references, index, table of authorities 
 Review Spelling and grammar with suggestions (English and Polish, by each run's language), thesaurus, word count, comments in margin balloons or a pane, track changes, accept/reject, compare documents, restrict editing, accessibility checker, document inspector 
 Mailings Mail merge from CSV, merge fields, address block, greeting line, rules, preview, finish to a document; envelopes and labels 
 View Print layout, web layout, draft, read mode, focus, zoom, one/multiple pages, page width, Navigation pane, rulers, gridlines, dark mode; interface in English, 简体中文, 繁體中文, 日本語, Português (Brasil), Español, Українська, Српски / Srpski, Eesti, Türkçe, Русский, Italiano, Deutsch, Polski, Čeština, Magyar, Français, Български, Tiếng Việt, 한국어, Svenska, Hrvatski, Nederlands, Dansk, Română, العربية (mirrored) Slovenščina or Bosanski (follows the system language by default) 
 Files .docx read/write, legacy 97-2003 .doc import, PDF export, .odt, .rtf, .html, .md, .tex, .txt import/export, page images 

The honest picture, area by area, is in ROADMAP.md, the
parity assessment and the generated
feature checklist.

install.title: Quick start
install.html:
git clone https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft
cd wordcraft
cargo run --release -p wordcraft -- --sample        # the desktop app with the sample document
cargo run --release -p wordcraft -- report.docx     # open a document

The interface translations and the spelling and hyphenation data come from craft-i18n, an optional build input. To build with them, check it out at the commit in craft-i18n.rev and point CRAFT_I18N_DIR at it (an absolute path); without it WordCraft builds with an English interface, English spelling falls back to an installed Hunspell English or craft-proof's built-in word list, and only Bulgarian, Turkish and Russian hyphenate (by rule):

git clone https://github.com/storytold/craft-i18n ../craft-i18n
git -C ../craft-i18n checkout "$(cat craft-i18n.rev)"
CRAFT_I18N_DIR="$PWD/../craft-i18n" cargo run --release -p wordcraft -- --sample

Command line:

wordcraft-cli convert report.docx report.pdf        # docx, pdf, odt, rtf, html, md, tex, txt, png
wordcraft-cli convert report.docx report.pdf --strict   # exit 3, no file, if a character or picture would be left out
wordcraft-cli text report.docx                      # plain text
wordcraft-cli inspect report.docx                   # structure as JSON
wordcraft-cli run --template sample \
  --cmd 'select.text={"text":"Membership"}' --cmd format.bold --save out.docx
wordcraft-cli run --script job.json                 # the same from a file: commands, then save to docx and pdf

convert --strict (a .pdf or .png output only) and render --strict (a PNG of one page) refuse a silently incomplete render: they exit 3 and write nothing if the output would draw a character no font has (an empty box) or leave out a picture. Exit codes are 0 (written), 1 (unreadable input, usage error, or --strict with another output type, checked before the input is read) and 3 (strict refusal). On exit 3, stderr has one wordcraft-cli: strict: … line per kind, then one JSON line:

wordcraft-cli convert in.docx out.pdf --strict
# wordcraft-cli: strict: 1 character cannot be drawn: U+2D30 (×3)
# wordcraft-cli: strict: 1 picture(s) left out: word/media/image2.bin (header2.xml): unsupported format
# {"schema":1,"strict":"failed","missing_glyphs":[{"cp":"U+2D30","count":3}],"missing_pictures":[{"part":"word/media/image2.bin","source_part":"word/header2.xml","reason":"unsupported_format"}],"truncated":false,"total_missing_glyphs":1,"total_missing_pictures":1,"glyphs_truncated":false,"pictures_truncated":false}

The JSON line (schema 1, also what file.strictReport returns) has schema, strict ("passed" or "failed"), missing_glyphs (entries {"cp", "count"}, sorted by code point), missing_pictures (entries {"part", "source_part", "reason"}: the picture's part or target, the story part it sits in such as word/header2.xml, and a reason code; source_part is also background (the page picture), body, header, footer, footnote, endnote, comment or text box where the part name is not known (a document not opened from a DOCX), or a chunk path such as word/afchunk1.docx > word/header1.xml for a picture inside an embedded DOCX chunk), truncated, the two totals total_missing_glyphs and total_missing_pictures, and glyphs_truncated and pictures_truncated for each list. The reason codes are missing_part, external_target, link_only, undecodable and unsupported_format; the stderr lines use plain words for them. When a list is cut, the stderr line gives the total (300 characters cannot be drawn (first 256 listed)). Each list stops at 256 entries separately; truncated is true when either was cut, and the totals count every distinct character and picture found, those past the cap included. Only characters the output draws count (not hidden text, or deleted text without --markup), and a character a fallback font draws is fine. Text inside a WMF or EMF picture counts too, shaped in the font the picture names with no fallback. A Private Use Area character fails only if no installed font maps it. The result depends on the fonts installed on the host (see #5624 for a fixed font set). An external picture target is never fetched: it is reported, not loaded. Pictures dropped when a DOCX is opened (a missing part, an external target, or a link only picture with no embedded copy) are reported for DOCX input only. They have no page, so a PNG of any page is also refused for a missing or external picture anywhere in the document, unused headers included. render --strict checks only the page it writes (--page; --scale doesn't matter), prints nothing on stdout when it refuses, and reports the same way. The engine takes strict: true on file.save, file.saveAs, file.exportPdf and file.exportPng, and file.strictReport {markup?, page?} returns the report without writing.

Web: cd apps/wordcraft-web && trunk serve, then open http://127.0.0.1:8771/?sample.
